guards.what: G2 (LIVE): a deck-level TRANSFORM fires Hook.ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck in C# and no deck-add hook in the sim, so a transformed-in Attack arrives UN-upgraded
guards.issue: MECHANISM: CardCmd.Transform on a **Deck** pile fires BOTH deck-add hooks -- `Hook.ModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck` (CardCmd.cs:427-434) and `Hook.AfterCardChangedPiles` (CardCmd.cs:447) -- because a transform replacement really does enter the deck. RunState.transform_card (run.py:406-465) fires NEITHER: it deletes the original and appends the replacement straight onto self.deck, bypassing run.add_card (run.py:341-354), which is the only place the sim dispatches either hook. REACHABILITY (LIVE, executed -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b09.py b09-molten / b09-fysh): with molten_egg held, `run.add_card(bash)` yields upgrade_level 1 (correct) but `run.transform_card(-> bash)` yields upgrade_level 0 where C# yields 1; with lucky_fysh held, transform_card grants 0 gold where C# grants 15. Both sides ported: deck transforms are reached by relic/astrolabe, relic/pandoras_box and the ported Wood Carvings / Nonupeipe content, and the conformance runner compares the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs (conformance/runner.py:618), so the missing upgrade is a parity failure and not merely a play-strength one. ONE mechanism at two sites in this batch (relic/lucky_fysh and relic/molten_egg) -- same verdict at both per binding rule 3; the fix is one call to the add_card hook pair from transform_card, not two relic fixes. Rule 7: leans on run.py and conformance/runner.py, neither hashed here.

guards.what: G3: `if (options.Flags.HasFlag(CardCreationFlags.NoHookUpgrades)) return false` (MoltenEgg.cs:27-30) has no counterpart in the sim, which has no card-creation flag concept
guards.rationale: MECHANISM NoHookUpgrades, one verdict at all THREE egg sites (relic/toxic_egg N1, relic/frozen_egg G2, relic/molten_egg G3) after the 2026-07-26 relic fix pass reconciled them -- they previously split two waivers against one gap on identical facts, which binding rule 3 forbids. VOCABULARY RULING (2026-07-26 relic fix pass), applied at every dead-in-the-source site in this tier so it stops contradicting itself. When a C# member the sim omits is DEAD IN THE GAME SOURCE ITSELF -- zero overrides, zero producers, zero callers anywhere under src/ -- the correct verdict is `faithful`, not `waiver`. PROMPT.md v6 item 3, which the relic stream itself wrote, settles the principle for the mirror-image case: 'a waiver is in-scope-adjacent and declined, and here there is no source behaviour to be faithful to.' A waiver claims something in scope was deliberately not audited; here there is nothing to decline, because the member provably cannot fire in any run of the shipping game and cannot become live by porting more content -- it would take a change to the game's own source. `faithful` also states the stronger and more useful fact: the two codebases have the SAME observable. Before this pass the relic tier split 8 waivers against 5 faithfuls on identical reasoning; these entries are now all `faithful` (binding rule 3). NOTE: this ruling does NOT touch MULTIPLAYER gates (`player != base.Owner`, `Players.Count == 1`), which stay `waiver` -- the shared contract names multiplayer as out of scope outright, and unlike a dead member a player count really can differ in the shipping game; the sim simply does not model that mode. AT THIS SITE the member is dead, and the grep is EXECUTED and exhaustive: `grep -rn NoHookUpgrades src/` returns exactly FOUR lines in the whole game source -- the enum member `NoHookUpgrades = 4` (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs:29) and the three egg relics READING it (FrozenEgg.cs:27, MoltenEgg.cs:27, ToxicEgg.cs:27). THREE READERS, ZERO PRODUCERS. The two composite flags that could set it indirectly are dead too: `grep -rn 'CardCreationFlags.NoUpgrades\b' src/` returns NOTHING, and `grep -rn NoModifications src/` returns only its own declaration (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs:68). `CardCreationOptions.Flags` has a private setter and is writable only through `WithFlags` (src/Core/Runs/CardCreationOptions.cs:57, 211-215), and all 29 `WithFlags` call sites were enumerated (`py audit/tools/relic_probes_b09.py b09-molten`) with the same result. So the guard can never be true for any card creation the shipping game performs. THIS ALSO RETRACTS relic/frozen_egg G2's stated dormancy trigger, which was 'porting any C# effect that creates cards WithFlags(NoHookUpgrades) -- the shape exists in the source's card-generation callers'. IT DOES NOT: no such caller exists anywhere under src/, so there is no unported content that would make this live, which is exactly what distinguishes a dead member from a dormant gap. The genuinely live sibling flag is `NoModifyHooks`, which HAS a real producer -- LastingCandy.cs:127 builds `WithFlags(CardCreationFlags.NoModifyHooks | CardCreationFlags.NoCardPoolModifications)` and CardFactory.cs:104 gates the whole `Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions` dispatch on it. That is a live C# path with no sim counterpart and it belongs to relic/lasting_candy's record, not to the eggs. Rule 7: src/Core/Runs/CardCreationFlags.cs, src/Core/Runs/CardCreationOptions.cs, src/Core/Factories/CardFactory.cs and src/Core/Models/Relics/LastingCandy.cs are cited and not hashed by this record.

guards.what: G4 (DORMANT): the sim applies Molten Egg's already-upgraded refusal to ALL THREE paths; C# applies it ONLY to the deck-add path, because EggRelicHelper.UpgradeValidCards has no upgrade-level check
guards.issue: MECHANISM: the reward and merchant paths both go through `EggRelicHelper.UpgradeValidCards(cards, CardType.Attack, this)` (MoltenEgg.cs:31, :39), whose only filter is `card.Type == cardType && card.IsUpgradable` (EggRelicHelper.cs:12-21) -- no level test. The `card.CurrentUpgradeLevel >= 1 -> return false` clause exists ONLY in TryModifyCardBeingAddedToDeck (MoltenEgg.cs:58-61). The sim puts the test in the shared `EggRelic._applies` predicate (relics/_eggs.py:34-37, `ONLY_UNUPGRADED`) and calls it from all three, so the sim refuses an already-upgraded Attack on the reward and merchant paths where C# would upgrade it again. REACHABILITY (DORMANT, executed census -- py audit/tools/relic_probes_b09.py b09-molten): **0 of the ported cards have max_upgrade_level > 1**, so a level-1 card is never IsUpgradable and BOTH sides skip it via the IsUpgradable clause they share; the extra ONLY_UNUPGRADED test is therefore unobservable today. Porting any card with MaxUpgradeLevel >= 2 makes it live -- the same population relic/archaic_tooth guard G1 in batch 1 is waiting on. Also worth recording as a near-miss of PROMPT.md bug class 19: molten_egg.py:12 and relics/_eggs.py:30 both cite "MoltenEgg.cs:56" for the already-upgraded refusal, but :56 is the `return false` of the IsUpgradable clause and the level check is at :58 -- the semantics are right and only the line number drifted. Rule 7: leans on relics/_eggs.py and EggRelicHelper.cs, neither hashed here.

guards.what: G5: C# swaps in a full CLONE and upgrades the clone (`newCard = base.Owner.RunState.CloneCard(card); CardCmd.Upgrade(newCard)`, MoltenEgg.cs:62-63); the sim upgrades the card IN PLACE and hands the same object back (relics/_eggs.py:47-51)
guards.rationale: PROMPT.md bug class 17 is a sim 'clone' that is really a shallow REBUILD and so drops enchantment, affliction and local cost modifiers. This site is the class checked and found to run the OTHER way: RunState.CloneCard is `ClonePreservingMutability()` + AddCard (RunState.cs:394-399), and mutating in place preserves strictly MORE per-instance state than any rebuild could -- there is nothing for the sim to lose. The resulting deck entry has the same id and the same upgrade level, which is what a replay compares (conformance/runner.py:618 diffs the deck as (id, upgrade_level) pairs), so binding rule 2's same-observable test is met. Two residues, both bookkeeping: C# registers the clone on the run via AddCard and leaves the ORIGINAL model in the card db, and C# routes the upgrade through CardCmd.Upgrade -- whose IsUpgradable guard (CardModel.cs:785-789) the sim's bare `Card.upgrade()` lacks (PROMPT.md bug class 14 / sweep D). The guard is not needed HERE because _applies already filters on `card.is_upgradable`, which is exactly why sweep D classifies both _eggs.py upgrade sites as dormant rather than as the astrolabe/bone_tea defect. Rule 7: leans on relics/_eggs.py, RunState.cs, CardModel.cs and conformance/runner.py, none hashed here.

guards.what: N1: `card.Owner != base.Owner` on the deck-add path and `player != base.Owner` on the other two (MoltenEgg.cs:24, 37, 46)
guards.rationale: Multiplayer-structural in all three places -- one player, so every card and every reward is the owner's. The bool return values are C#'s 'I modified the collection' signal for the AfterModifyingRewards callbacks; the sim's hooks return None or the replacement card and have nothing to signal.

guards.what: N2: `card.Type != CardType.Attack` (MoltenEgg.cs:50) and the type passed to UpgradeValidCards (lines 31, 39)
guards.rationale: CARD_TYPE = CardType.ATTACK (molten_egg.py:16) on all three paths, matching all three C# sites. Recorded explicitly because the sts2 egg-to-type mapping is NOT the sts1 one -- Toxic is Skill, Frozen is Power, Molten is Attack -- and relics/_eggs.py's own module docstring flags it as the trap. Verified against the sibling sources rather than assumed.

CardModel.IsUpgradable is `CurrentUpgradeLevel < MaxUpgradeLevel` (CardModel.cs:785-789), which the sim's is_upgradable mirrors, and it is the clause that keeps the egg off the 35 ported cards with max_upgrade_level == 0 (every curse and status). Present on all three sim paths and on all three C# paths (the other two via UpgradeValidCards' own IsUpgradable test).

guards.what: N4: the sim has ONE modify_card_reward_options pass where C# runs TryModifyCardRewardOptions and then TryModifyCardRewardOptions**Late** as two complete passes
guards.issue: MECHANISM: Hook.TryModifyCardRewardOptions (Hook.cs:1445-1468) walks every listener's non-Late override and then walks every listener's Late override, so a Late modifier is guaranteed to see the finished output of every plain one. Molten Egg is a LATE modifier (MoltenEgg.cs:21), which matters for an UPGRADER: running last means the upgrade is applied to whatever card the plain-phase relics finally settled on. The sim has a single flat pass over run.relics (rewards.py:297-301) with no phase structure. This is audit/records/seam/hook_dispatch.json gap G3 (the missing Late phase) at a second site, carrying that record's verdict per binding rule 3, and the same shape as relic/brilliant_scarf guard G2 on the energy-cost hook. DORMANT at this site: a divergence needs a ported plain-phase modify_card_reward_options listener whose output Molten Egg's upgrade depends on -- i.e. one that REPLACES a reward card with a different one -- and the ported listeners either upgrade, enchant or add to the same list. Porting a plain-phase relic that swaps a reward card's identity makes it live. Rule 7: leans on rewards.py and Hook.cs, neither hashed here.
